name: BNYX
notes: ⚠ `low` is not a judgement on the name — it is the research's own verdict. His identity, era, credits and commercial standing are firmly sourced (the Yeat catalogue, "Meltdown", *Pink Tape*, a #1 with "Slime You Out", Complex's Best Hip-Hop Producer Alive 2023), but the paragraph marks **every parametric bullet** `[LOW-CONF]` because no interview documenting his method was reachable. So the honest reading of this file is: the shape below is inference from the records, and the sourced part is only that he is the load-bearing distortion producer of this lane's current era. INFERRED here means all of it — bpm, drums, 808, melody and arrangement. Within that, the parameters the research does name are the ones this model leans on hardest: "heavily overdriven 808 with an audible harmonic buzz ... sitting at or above the vocal in perceived loudness" is `distortion` heavy at 0.6–0.9 wet, the widest wet range in this batch; "clipped and narrow" with "long noise/impact layers replacing conventional fills" is a compressed high `velocityTiers` block plus `percs.lanes` of `impact` and `reverse` rather than any tuned percussion; "single detuned synth or bell motif, 2 bars ... extremely low note density" is 1–3 notes a bar on a 2-pitch-to-3-pitch motif at `timbreHint` `detuned_bell`; and "static i with a single chromatic upper voice" is `halfStepDissonance` 0.5 against `chordToneBias` 0.36 over a two-family harmony. The "bed of pitched noise" is the `sustain_pad` sitting alongside the two required counter styles. "Frequent late beat switch on album cuts" is `switchUpProb` 0.45. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 844 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 889/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, arp, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 914/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.22 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 914/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide. ⚠ `melody.emptyBarBias` reduced again, 0.1 → 0.04, after the countermelody was still short of the 980 floor. An empty bar yields an empty counter region and every empty region is identical, so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. ⚠ `melody.emptyBarBias` removed entirely (was 0.04). Even at 0.04 it held the countermelody just under the 980 floor: an empty bar gives the counter nothing to answer and every empty answer is identical, so a model this close to the line cannot afford any. The lead keeps its space through density and phrasing instead, which vary per seed — silence does not. ⚠ **`countermelody.styles` weight on `sustain_pad` cut from 3 to 1**, which is what was actually saturating the counter (this model reached 959/1000 against a floor of 980). A probe over 1000 seeds showed the collisions were almost all ONE-NOTE counters: a single note at tick 240 held for the whole clip. That is the pad over a one-chord vamp — `maxChords` 2, `harmonicRhythm` weighted to `vamp`, `chordDurationBeats` running to the length of the clip — and `pad_notes` writes one note per chord event, so the only things a seed can vary are its pitch and whether it breathes. About a fifth of all seeds landed in that space and collided with each other. The pad is a **bed**, which is what this file already called it, not the counter’s usual answer; at weight 1 it is still there and the answering styles carry the rest. ⛔ The deeper gap is in the engine and is logged as `TASK-165`: a pad held as a single note across eight bars is not what a pad does, and every drone model in volumes 2–5 will meet this.
